problem: Existing RGB-based navigation only achieves coarse, ~1 m success, while precise-positioning methods need depth, LiDAR, maps or NeRFs. As a result the mobile manipulator's base ends up outside its manipulation policy's demonstration distribution.
motivation: Manipulation policies only work reliably when the base pose lies within the distribution of their demonstrations, so centimeter/degree-level base positioning is needed. RGB cameras are cheap and universal, and collecting real-world demonstrations is costly. The paper therefore asks whether a policy trained on one object instance can generalize to a whole category.
key_idea: Ground the target object with language-driven segmentation (OwlV2+SAM2), compare masked frozen DINOv2 features of current and goal views via a 64x64 cosine-similarity score matrix, and decode discrete base actions, with a rule-based mask-alignment stop.
insight: Explicit object grounding is essential: DinoTxtAttention without segmentation gets 0% success. The explicit score matrix beats cross-attention (DinoAttention) on unseen instances, suggesting that a dense correspondence map transfers geometry from one instance to a category. The learned policy struggles to output stop consistently because of noisy demo terminal states, so the auxiliary IoU/center-of-mass stop is needed to convert navigation into success. Most failures come from unstable segmentation, especially in dim lighting.
method: Problem formulation: behavioral cloning of a policy mapping (current 4-view RGB, goal multi-view RGB, text prompt) to discrete actions; each of x, y, theta has 3 levels (-/0/+), step 0.2 m / 12 deg
Vision encoder: frozen DINOv2 (with registers) gives 34x34x1024 embeddings for each image
Segmentation module: OwlV2 detects the prompted object to produce a box; SAM2 refines it to a mask; embeddings are cropped and masked to the target

Action decoder: box coordinates are encoded by an MLP into a 4096-d embedding; masked embeddings are pooled to 8x8, and a 64x64 cosine-similarity score matrix is computed and flattened; concatenated with the box embedding and fed to an MLP with three 3-class heads
Auxiliary stopping: inference-time override to stop when mask IoU with goal > 0.6 and center-of-mass x difference < 25 px

Data: 715 automated expert trajectories on a Spot with AprilTag localization, using a single green chair; pseudo-goals sampled from future frames of the same trajectory; varied radial distance, approach angle and start heading

Evaluation: edge-alignment (translation <=0.3 m and orientation within +-8 deg of GT) and object-alignment (translation <=0.3 m and mask center-of-mass distance to goal <= max over training final observations)

setting.backbone: Frozen DINOv2 encoder + OwlV2 + SAM2 (frozen), trained MLP action decoder on the score matrix
setting.training_data: 715 real-world automated expert trajectories of Spot approaching a single green chair in one indoor environment; pseudo-goal relabeling from future frames
setting.observation: 4-view RGB (front stitched from two cameras, left, right, back) plus goal images and text prompt; no depth, LiDAR or map
setting.action_space: discrete low-level base motion: x/y/theta each in {-,0,+}, 0.2 m translation / 12 deg rotation
setting.privileged: Goal observation images are required at test time; ground-truth pose from Spot AprilTag localization is used only for evaluation and expert data generation

results: DinoScoreAux reaches 94% (edge) / 96.67% (object) success on the seen chair and 74.58% / 89.42% on unseen chairs, beating the DinoAttention(Aux) and DinoTxtAttention (0%) baselines. It generalizes to unseen environments (85%/95% outdoor, 79%/91% indoor average) and to other categories (suitcases 0.91/0.96, drawer organizers 0.60/0.73).
limitations: Depends heavily on segmentation quality; masks flicker or fail in dim or challenging lighting (a scenario with dim lighting got 0%)
Assumes the target stays in view with no occluding obstacles, and requires a goal observation image

Precision is limited by Spot's actuation (0.2 m / 12 deg steps, 0.3 m and 8 deg tolerances); the learned policy cannot stop reliably without a hand-crafted rule; tested only on Spot with few categories
